summary: All seven fix_tasks close, re-verified by own reads and runs: the outbound engine now transmits, retries to a bound and hard-discards, with real tests proving each path.
notes: SECOND-ROUND VERDICT: approve. contract-check re-run on the FINAL diff (25 files, +1656/-134): ok=true, 0 violations, not_checked: forbid.behaviors (re-evaluated by hand below). 25 of 28 files and 1790 of 3200 total diff lines; every per_class cap respected. All seven fix_tasks from the first round are closed, and I re-verified each one by my own reads and my own test runs rather than trusting the report.

CLOSURE 1 of 7 (the engine that was missing entirely) - VERIFIED REAL. Drenar now runs two ordered passes against one 'ahora': descartarExpiradas hard-discards expired rows, then intentarPendientes SELECTs pending non-expired rows (salida.go:149) and transmits each through the injected Transmisor. TransmisorWhatsmeow (transmisor.go:43-71) is a genuine implementation calling cliente.SendMessage and returning only respuesta.ID. Retry accounting is real: registrarFallo increments intentos and, at nuevoIntentos >= intentosMaximos, DELETEs the row and logs EventoSalidaAgotada; otherwise it UPDATEs intentos and logs EventoSalidaReintentada. Both previously-dead constants are now on live paths. Wired in main.go:105 via bucleDeDrenajeSalida, a ticker goroutine cancelled on shutdown - the '_ = colaSalida' discard is gone.

I RAN THE GO OUTBOX SUITE MYSELF: all tests pass, and the engine tests are honest rather than tautological. TestDrenarTransmiteYMarcaEnviado proves one transmit call, the correlation id persisted, and - decisively - that a SECOND Drenar does not re-transmit an already-sent row (idempotent replay proven, not asserted). TestDrenarReintentaHastaElLimiteYAbandonaSinColaDeReenvio uses intentosMaximos=2 and walks the real arithmetic: after drain 1 the row is alive with intentos=1, after drain 2 the row is GONE with exactly 2 transmitter calls, and a third drain finds nothing to retry - which simultaneously proves the bound, the hard discard, the absence of a dead-letter row and the absence of any re-enqueue. TestDrenarNuncaTransmiteUnMensajeYaExpirado proves TTL wins the race against retry: an expired row reaches the transmitter zero times and is still discarded. I checked the bound arithmetic independently: with intentosMaximos=N the row is deleted on the Nth failure, so exactly N transmit attempts occur, which is the correct reading of 'at most the configured number'.

NO DEAD-LETTER PATH SMUGGLED IN - re-verified after the engine landed, since this was the highest-risk regression. There is no quarantine table, no startup recovery query, no second table beyond cola_salida, and no re-enqueue on failure: exhaustion DELETEs. A grep for dead-letter/dlq/cuarentena/quarantine/startup_recovery across the sidecar returns exactly one hit, and it is the prohibitive comment at salida.go:82 stating those mechanisms do not exist. The retry path keeps the SAME row and updates its counter, which is recovery, not re-enqueue.

CLOSURE 2 of 7 (binding human ruling 3) - VERIFIED. docs/STATUS.md gains a Pendiente entry 'Servidor del socket IPC en Go, ausente' that is unusually honest: it states no net.Listen/ListenUnix/Accept exists in sidecar/, that HEX-017's verification therefore stays at wire and library level with no real end-to-end loop, that this is declared structural debt belonging to plan task 3, and that it blocks task 15's live-channel tests. The TTL cross-reference was also added to the pre-existing calibration entry, naming the ratified 900000 default and its single source in configuracion.TtlSalidaMsPorOmision.

CLOSURE 3 of 7 (the silent-discard defect) - VERIFIED AND WELL REASONED. adaptador.rs:402 replaces the 0 sentinel with '.ok_or(ErrorCanalWhatsmeow::OrigenDesconocido)?', and the connection check was reordered ahead of it (adaptador.rs:385) with a comment that correctly notes enviar_saliente re-checks the connection, so the reorder only prioritises which rejection surfaces when both apply rather than replacing the later guard. The load-bearing comment articulates the exact defect I flagged: a 0 would read sidecar-side as 'already expired' and burn the message with zero real send attempts, indistinguishable from a legitimate expiry. Covered by tests/salida.rs send_sin_marca_de_origen_conocida_devuelve_error_explicito, which I ran. Worth recording that this error is near-unreachable in the real flow: a reply requires a TestigoDeEntrante derived from an inbound event, and the same read loop that delivers that event populates the map, so the entry always exists within a process lifetime. It is a correct fail-loud guard for a state that should not occur, not a path the core will routinely hit.

CLOSURE 4 of 7 (unbounded map) - VERIFIED, and the tests are sharper than required. MarcasDeOrigen (adaptador.rs:56) pairs a HashMap with a VecDeque insertion order and evicts FIFO at CAPACIDAD_MAXIMA_MARCAS_DE_ORIGEN = 10_000, with a doc comment that correctly ties the bound to the NFR-01 budget. Two unit tests, both of which I ran: one proves the cap holds and the five oldest are the ones purged; the second proves that UPDATING an existing conversation does not count as a new insertion - which is the subtle bug a naive implementation would ship (pushing to the deque on every update would evict live conversations while the map stayed under cap). Testing that second property was not asked for and is the right instinct.

CLOSURE 5 of 7 (doc/ADR coherence) - VERIFIED. Protocol section 6 now opens 'Once tipos.' matching its eleven-row table, and adr-0011 item 2 now reads 'versión 4 de cable (actualizada por HEX-017, 2026-08-09), con once tipos de mensajes cerrados ... (versión 1.3)'. The update is an annotation carrying its own date, not a rewrite of the original decision, so the ADR discipline of superseding rather than editing history is respected.

CLOSURE 6 of 7 (duplicated defaults) - VERIFIED. outbox.TtlPorOmision and IntentosMaximosPorOmision are now aliases of configuracion.TtlSalidaMsPorOmision and configuracion.IntentosMaximosSalidaPorOmision (salida.go:19-20), so the literals 900000 and 3 exist in exactly one place, with a comment saying recalibration means editing one site. Drenar's signature dropped the bypassable ttlMs parameter and now always measures against the constructor-set c.ttlMs (salida.go:87-88).

CLOSURE 7 of 7 (per-message expiry log) - VERIFIED. descartarExpiradas uses DELETE ... RETURNING id_mensaje and emits one EventoSalidaExpirada line per discarded message carrying its own id_evento, replacing the aggregate count. TestDescartarExpiradosRegistraUnaLineaPorMensaje asserts exactly two lines for two expired messages and that each id appears - so the anti-ban audit trail can now name which message was lost. ContadorExpiradas is still incremented, now by the counted rows.

SENTINEL RE-VERIFIED UNDER THE NEW SEND PATH, and it is now MORE meaningful than before. The watch list gained 'Transmitir' with its own synthetic case, and the self-test expectation rose 1 to 2, so every newly watched name has a case proving it is caught. Crucially, transmisor.go now contains a REAL cliente.SendMessage call - the first one ever to exist in the sidecar - and TestCentinelaSinRutasDeEnvioFueraDelOutbox still passes because the exemption at line 84 skips the outbox directory. Before this task the guard watched names that nothing called; it now genuinely exercises its exemption boundary. Both sentinel tests pass in my own run, and the empty-corpus guard and directory exemption are untouched.

STALE MODULE DOC (flagged by the orchestrator) - VERIFIED ACCURATE. The adaptador.rs header now describes send as forwarding over wire v4 to the sidecar's outbound queue, returning Aceptado once the frame is written, with 'accepted for later delivery' materialised by the queue's absolute TTL and bounded retries, and states the HEX-015 in-memory bridge was replaced with its historical record kept in adr-0011. Every clause matches the code I read. The estado_ventana / adr-0010 TYPE-vs-POLICY paragraph is preserved unchanged.

PLANTILLA ADJUDICATION UNCHANGED FROM ROUND ONE - the wrapper decision remains the honest resolution, and the fix round did not disturb it. escenario_de_asimetria_de_plantilla and send_plantilla_devuelve_error_representable both still pass in my own run, so the contract battery keeps exercising the port's TYPE asymmetry while a dedicated test keeps pinning the real adapter's Err(PlantillaNoRepresentable). Coverage stays split rather than removed, which is what distinguishes this from the HEX-015 defect class.

FIRST-ROUND STRENGTHS RE-CONFIRMED INTACT: TTL still anchored to the persisted origin timestamp with the verdict verified identical across a database reopen; both idempotency primitives (ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING, UPDATE ... WHERE enviado_en_ms IS NULL) unchanged and now actually consumed by the engine; HEX-015 bridge fully absent; protocol sections 1-9 present and in order with versions consistent end to end (Go and Rust both 4); acks carrying id_correlacion with the transport-identifier guard passing; AC-10 re-deferral honest in both STATUS and adr-0011.

TRANSMITTER PRIVACY VERIFIED AT THE UNIT LEVEL: TestTransmisorWhatsmeowResuelveDireccionYEnviaSoloElTexto deliberately sets a SendResponse.Sender JID different from the destination and asserts only the ID is returned, so the Sender JID provably never escapes Transmitir. Address resolution reuses the pre-existing identidad.Almacen.DireccionDe (identidad.go:439, unmodified and not in the touch list), so no forbidden file was reached to enable this.

No traffic-shaping folklore: a case-insensitive scan across all .go and .rs files returns a single hit, the prohibitive comment at salida.go:197 stating the retry has no wait, no jitter and no schedule - only a failure ceiling. All new identifiers, comments and doc comments are Spanish; dates absolute; no new third-party dependency in either the Rust workspace or the Go module (ClienteWhatsmeow and ResolutorDeDirecciones are locally declared interfaces over types already present); banco.rs, bateria.rs and all other forbidden files untouched.

RESIDUAL (non-blocking, accepted) - nothing runs end to end. The Go IPC socket server does not exist, so the Rust client writes mensaje_saliente frames that only the simulated sidecar reads, and the Go queue is exercised only as a library against SQLite. Each half is well tested in isolation and the two halves are never integrated. This is human-ruled out of scope and now honestly declared in STATUS as task 3's structural debt, but it is the reason functional_risk is judged on unintegrated components: the first real integration happens at plan task 15.

RESIDUAL (non-blocking, accepted) - intervaloDrenajeSalida = 2s is a hardcoded const in main.go rather than a configuration parameter. The contract forbade hiding the TTL and the retry BOUND, not the loop cadence, and the comment explicitly distinguishes it as mechanical loop pacing rather than a calibration or anti-ban parameter. It nonetheless shapes real retry pacing (a 3-attempt series resolves in roughly 6 seconds), so it is worth promoting to configuration when task 14's behavioural discipline lands and starts competing for the same TTL budget.

RESIDUAL (non-blocking, pre-existing) - cola_salida lives in outbox.db, which remains outside the four databases covered by the A-2 backup contract. The blueprint recorded this and the task did not widen the backup contract, so an outbound message pending at backup time is not captured. Given the 15-minute TTL the exposure window is inherently small, but it should be stated rather than discovered later.

RESIDUAL (non-blocking, cosmetic) - cola_salida's columns carry no NOT NULL constraints, unlike the sibling outbox table in the same file which declares them. Nothing in the current code inserts a NULL, and id_mensaje UNIQUE is what ON CONFLICT needs, so this is schema laxity rather than a defect. ContadorExpiradas is also a package-level global shared across queue instances; the test reads it as a delta rather than an absolute, which is the correct handling.
